fun_fact: From hugging trees in the Himalayas to sitting before bulldozers, India has a long history of grassroots environmental movements. The Chipko movement of the 1970s — where villagers, many of them women, hugged trees to stop them being felled — sparked a wave of people-led struggles like Appiko and the Narmada Bachao Andolan. That spirit lives on today in protests over the Aravallis, Great Nicobar and Ken-Betwa, where ordinary people still stand up for forests, rivers and coasts.
author: Simran
